title: How a Pune proptech cut cost-per-site-visit 61% by killing junk leads at the form
content: SITUATION: A Pune proptech selling 2BHK flats in Hinjewadi and Wakad spent ₹6.2L/month across Meta and Google lead-gen, pulling 3,400 leads at ₹182 CPL. CPL looked elite; the funnel was rotting. Only 9% of leads answered calls, just 41 booked site visits, and ~60% were job-seekers and brokers chasing a misleading 'flats from ₹25 lakh' creative. Real cost-per-site-visit: a brutal ₹15,100. ACTION: We fixed quality at the source, not the call sheet. Killed Meta Instant Forms (the junk magnet) and switched to click-to-WhatsApp with a 3-question qualifier bot: budget, possession timeline, target locality. Added a deliberate 'min budget ₹40L' line in creative to repel tyre-kickers. Moved 35% of spend into high-intent Google Search ('ready-to-move flats Wakad', 'RERA 2BHK Hinjewadi') and paused Justdial, which only recycled broker leads. OUTCOME: Over 8 weeks, leads fell to 1,950 but answer-rate jumped 9%→34%, site visits climbed from 41 to 96/month, and cost-per-site-visit dropped to ₹5,900 (down 61%). Bookings doubled from 3 to 7/month on the same ₹6.2L budget.
lesson: In real estate, CPL is a vanity metric — a ₹182 lead that never picks up costs more than a ₹600 one that books. Optimize for cost-per-qualified-conversation, not cost-per-lead. A WhatsApp qualifier bot plus a deliberately 'scary' price floor in the creative does the sales team's first call for them: it pushes unqualified buyers out before they ever hit the call sheet, so fewer, hotter leads convert at 4x the rate.
